dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Those 17 records have effective dates from 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-28, so they were posted later than their effective event dates."

"Late posting is a recurring pattern, not unique to this cluster: 54 rows have different effective and posting dates, all are renewals, and their posting dates are month-end dates (31 Mar, 30 Apr, 31 May, 30 Jun)."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Confidence: medium-high. The extract supports no material issue, although entitlement-posting linkage is not independently available."
"This cannot prove intent was absent, but it provides no basis for escalation."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The extract has no region column, so ‘West’ cannot be independently verified; a dealer master mapping DLR-104 and DLR-219 to region would confirm scope."

"Place a reversible hold on any restatement or deletion of the 17 records, annotate them as month-end dealer timing, and obtain the two DealerDrop accepted-row manifests plus entitlement-posting confirmation."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not escalate as duplicate revenue or manipulated reporting."
"Reconcile by `source_event_id` before changing the trend pack or ledger."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The corresponding May batches reconcile exactly" is supported at batch level, but row-level linkage of the 17 recharge records to DF-00020 and DF-00040 is inferred rather than directly evidenced; the submission appropriately acknowledges this limitation.

"The flagged 17 annual renewals are best explained by an expected month-end dealer batch-posting process" is well supported, but the word "expected" relies partly on an operational email that is corroboration rather than independent proof.
"No material issue" remains conditional because entitlement-posting linkage is absent; it should not be read as ruling out an entitlement or GL impact.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: An entitlement or GL-posting mismatch could still make the event materially problematic despite unique source IDs and reconciled dealer cash batches. The analyst handled this alternative by identifying the missing entitlement evidence and making confirmation a decision-changing next step. The analyst also considered duplicate revenue, a May-only pipeline defect, and manipulated reporting.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and join the DealerDrop accepted-row manifests and entitlement/GL posting records to the 17 recharge records by `source_event_id`, then document the reconciliation result directly rather than relying on inferred batch linkage.

"In the post-launch matched window, 502 of 904 South Nova-S1 sessions were marked `RESOLVED`, but 193 were `ABANDONED`, 168 were `ERROR`, and only 41 were `TRANSFERRED`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The pilot is associated with fewer CareDesk tickets, but the evidence is also consistent with complaints being contained, abandoned, errored, or excluded before case creation."
"Whether CareDesk case-creation rules changed at pilot launch, especially for pre-authentication sessions."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Do not treat the South complaint decline as proof that NovaIVR improved customer experience."
"Whether ‘RESOLVED’ means a verified customer outcome or only successful IVR completion."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally yet."
"Keep national rollout paused and continue the South pilot with a reversible monitoring hold."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "publish a daily matched dashboard containing all IVR sessions (including pre-authentication errors and abandonments), CareDesk cases, repeat contacts, service-event exposure, and outcomes by region."
"What exact date and routing configuration made a South session eligible for `NOVA-S1`, and what were the daily eligible-session denominators from 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-26?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "South service pressure did not decrease" is somewhat overstated because service-event counts and affected-account estimates are proxies for pressure and do not by themselves establish customer friction or complaint volume.

"Expand only after two complete weeks show no unexplained loss in customer outcomes" is a reasonable operational safeguard, but the two-week threshold and the definition of acceptable unexplained loss are not evidence-based in the submission.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative: the pilot may have genuinely improved self-service, with some sessions resolved without cases. This remains appropriately unresolved because `RESOLVED` is not shown to mean a verified customer outcome. The analyst also considered changed routing exposure and case-creation rules as alternatives.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link individual IVR sessions to subsequent CareDesk cases, repeat contacts, callbacks, and verified outcomes—including abandoned and errored sessions—and report these rates by pilot status and region before making any expansion decision.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Submission states: “The file has only 4 event rows, covering 4 distinct inverters (`INV-17`, `INV-03`, `INV-22`, `INV-09`) across 2026-05-27 09:42 to 2026-06-04 16:18,” citing `inverter_events.csv`, rows 2–5 and timestamp/inverter fields.
Submission separately cites `severity`, `cleared`, `impact_mw`, and `duration_min` for the claim that all events cleared, had zero impact, and lasted 1–7 minutes.
The conclusion is explicitly scoped to “the observed events” and “this file,” distinguishing observation from fleet-level inference.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: Submission identifies the warning as `COMM_LINK_WARN`, notes that it was cleared with zero reported impact, and avoids treating event wording as proof of equipment failure or intent.

It recognizes the key alternative explanation that the extract may be incomplete or that fields may be defaulted/masked, and proposes checking query metadata, expected fleet count, and field provenance.
Reasoning is primarily based on one event file and does not independently triangulate against telemetry, alarms, or export data; this limits the score to 3 rather than 4.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly states that the file lacks “site, fleet-size, or export-scope” fields, so it does not support a fleet conclusion.
It says equipment failure or material impact is “not supported by this file,” rather than claiming those conditions are impossible.

It specifies decision-changing uncertainty and a bounded check: “obtain the export query metadata or a row count plus expected fleet/inverter count” and verify whether `impact_mw` and `cleared` are populated from the source.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation “Do not escalate on the observed events” follows the reported facts: one warning, three informational events, all cleared, zero MW impact, and short durations.
The proposed check is cheap and reversible, and escalation is conditioned on concrete findings: incompleteness or systematically masked fields.
The action preserves an appropriate operational safeguard without searching for an unsupported story.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The scoped conclusion—“Do not escalate on the observed events”—matches the visible evidence and the exercise requirement not to invent a plant problem from a short communications warning.
The analyst appropriately avoids a fleet-wide conclusion because the extract has only four rows and no fleet or export-scope metadata.
The conclusion remains conditional on a completeness and field-validity check, which is a defensible qualification rather than overreach.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the events have durations of 1–7 minutes is traceable if the cited CSV values are accurate, but the submission does not reproduce the individual durations, so the claim is less independently auditable than the other claims.

“Do not escalate” is sensible for the observed event records, but the submission does not state whether any separate operational policy requires escalation of communications warnings regardless of MW impact.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extract may be incomplete, limited to a narrow query, or have `impact_mw` and `cleared` populated by defaults or masking. Under that interpretation, the reassuring event summary would not establish fleet-wide absence of impact; the proposed metadata, row-count, expected-fleet, and field-provenance checks would discriminate it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add one independent cross-check—such as source alarm/telemetry records or export data for the same timestamps—to confirm that the zero-MW and cleared fields reflect actual operational state rather than reporting defaults.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “Recomputed over all 96 blocks per day using 0.25 hours per block” is tied to dispatch_blocks.csv fields submitted_schedule_mw and actual_mw.
The penalty calculation is explicitly tied to dsm_penalty_rs in dispatch_blocks.csv and corroborated by AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md.
The analyst distinguishes the displayed commercial-rate reconstruction from recorded penalties and identifies the reconciliation gap using DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: “It does not establish that the wind-stow pilot caused a 31.6% reduction” correctly identifies the different-day comparison as a causal limitation.
The analyst constructs a same-day counterfactual using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on the 12 pilot_revision rows.
The submission considers innocent alternative explanations including wind, forecast accuracy, actual generation, cloud conditions, settlement details, and selection of revised blocks.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Confidence is claim-specific: “high for arithmetic, medium for the operational association, low-medium for causality.”
The analyst states that only one conventional day and one AI-assisted day are compared and that the data cannot separate pilot effects from day-specific conditions.
The recommendation identifies decision-changing evidence: repeated matched observations, shadow counterfactuals, and full settlement reconciliation.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot in high-wind conditions with monitoring; do not treat this result alone as grounds for broad expansion” preserves potential operational value without overclaiming.
The proposed repeated, pre-specified comparison preserves the base schedule as a shadow counterfactual and records accepted revisions.
The rollback option and reconciliation to final meter and settlement records are proportionate safeguards.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately retains the observed 31.6% two-day penalty difference while rejecting the unsupported claim that the pilot caused it.
It reports the smaller same-day schedule-error improvement: 325.2825 MWh under the base schedule versus 282.7625 MWh using the submitted schedule.
The conclusion is appropriately scoped to an association and recommends continued testing rather than either broad expansion or dismissal of the pilot.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claim identified. The recommendation to continue the pilot in high-wind conditions is a decision under uncertainty rather than a causal claim, and it is appropriately paired with monitoring, rollback, and limits on expansion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May improvement may primarily reflect day-specific wind, forecast, cloud, generation, or settlement conditions, or the selective timing of the 12 revised blocks, rather than the pilot itself. The submission explicitly preserves this alternative because the comparison is based on different days and only one pilot day.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed repeated matched high-wind/stow evaluation with a frozen base schedule as a block-level shadow counterfactual, while reconciling both schedules to final meter and settlement data under the complete DSM formula.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"The current product master maps P1001 to HS6 `902110`, legacy NOVA `902110`, and Helios `90211090`..."
"The Swiss tariff matrix maps P1001 / Hip implant to approved CN8 `90211000`, effective from 2025-01-01, and explicitly labels it “Swiss local nomenclature.”"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "The declaration is demonstrably wrong because it differs from Helios `90211090` — rejected: the Swiss matrix uses `90211000` for the same P1001 product..."
"The packet contains a product or origin mismatch — rejected by the matching P1001 description, US origin, and CHF 126,900 value across the declaration and invoice."
"A ruling that assigns a different code, or evidence that `90211000` was not effective on 2025-11-04, would change the disposition..."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Confidence: medium-high; legal correctness still requires confirmation from the current Swiss Tares/ruling source."
"The matrix warns that it is a working classification, not a consolidated legal ruling database."
"The current Swiss Tares classification or product-specific customs ruling is not supplied."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios uses CN8 `90211090`, while the Swiss matrix assigns Swiss local code `90211000` to P1001."
"The matrix ... explicitly labels it “Swiss local nomenclature.”"
"The canonical schema also does not record code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates, or ruling authority."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate CH-2025-000522 as a likely declaration error based on this automated flag."
"Suppress or annotate this automated alert as a cross-system-code mismatch without changing the accepted declaration."
"Perform one targeted validation against the current Swiss Tares/ruling record for P1001 and the filing date; escalate only if that authoritative check disagrees with `90211000`."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The declaration therefore agrees with the available Swiss reference" is appropriately limited to the available working matrix, but it could more explicitly state that the matrix does not establish legal correctness; the submission otherwise supplies that limitation and a targeted authoritative check.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss local code could still be legally incorrect if the current Tares classification, a product-specific ruling, or the code's filing-date effectiveness differs from the working matrix; the submission identifies and preserves this alternative rather than treating the mismatch as conclusively benign.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the current Swiss Tares or product-specific ruling record for P1001, including the applicable nomenclature version and effective date, before operationally suppressing the alert.

dimensions.name: Decision safety

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported factual claim is apparent. The statement that a "customs ruling supporting Ireland/preference would change the claim from unsupported to supportable" is conditional and appropriately presented as potentially relevant, but its relevance would depend on the applicable preference regime and ruling scope.

Alternatively, the applicable preference rule may support the claim through a qualifying origin route despite United States manufacturing; the submission correctly identifies that the rule and issuing authority are missing.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Tie the requested supplier evidence and review decision to the specific applicable preferential-origin rule and identify the exact required document format, issuer, validity period, and governing authority.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission states that all rows carry a QCore snapshot timestamp at 2026-07-31 02:10, but it does not distinguish this snapshot field from the distribution of qcore_release_ts values or test whether release timestamps are concentrated at that hour.

The claim that the 39.4-hour median mixes exception/hold-related records is plausible from the stated dataset context, but the submission does not show a specific comparison excluding exceptions or quantify the effect.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent cycle time may be inflated or otherwise distorted by QCore interface-commit timing rather than reflecting the actual authorization or disposition decision time. The submission's request for authorization audit timestamps would help test this, but it does not explicitly profile qcore_release_ts by hour or identify interface timing as a competing mechanism.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Profile qcore_release_ts by hour and reconcile a targeted set of routine released batches to QCore authorization/decision audit events and SOP evidence-ready timestamps, while explicitly checking that QCore and LabTrack data are not being treated as a single point-in-time snapshot.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “Total apparent value is $152,558.03 across 24 OPEN requests; total requested quantity is 29.” Source: part_requests.csv, rows 2–25, with stated filter and aggregation.
“Exact joins on manufacturer_part_no, revision_required=revision, and uom produce clear positive-stock candidates.” Sources: part_requests.csv and spare_parts.csv, with relevant fields identified.
“The inventory snapshot is not demonstrably current.” Sources: source_freshness.csv and maintenance_email.txt.

The submission gives file, field, and sometimes row-level references and acknowledges stale-source counterevidence, but it does not provide row-level support for each candidate classification or value subtotal.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “Description variation is the main blocker, so semantic search is required before any value can be found” — rejected because exact part-number/revision/UOM matching identifies positive-stock candidates.

“Every catalog hit is an avoidable purchase” — rejected because the servo-drive example is reserved for a safety-critical filler and policy requires qualification, reservation, and engineering confirmation.
“Positive available_qty_global means actionable stock now” — rejected because freshness is stale and global availability can lag local reservation.

The analysis separates retrieval from transferability and triangulates identifiers, restrictions, reservations, and freshness. It could be stronger by explicitly testing whether semantic matching finds additional candidates beyond the exact-join set.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “I call $0 (0%) actionable now because the stock source is stale and the email warns that global availability may lag local reservations.”
“I classify $52,961.31 (34.7%) as needing engineering and live-availability validation, and $99,596.72 (65.3%) as not transferable from current evidence.”
“This could move some of the $52,961.31 from ‘needs check’ to actionable.”

The submission distinguishes apparent, candidate, validated, and actionable value; ties confidence to source freshness and missing engineering/reservation evidence; and uses a conservative operational boundary.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Do not cancel requests or place transfers yet.”
“Run a reversible exact-join queue using the candidate rows above, hold candidate stock pending live reservation and receiving-site checks, and label semantic matches as suggestions only.”
“Reassess the avoidable-value estimate after the fresh snapshot; build a semantic-search pilot only if unmatched requests remain after identifier cleanup.”

The recommendation is reversible, protects against unsafe transfers and overstated savings, prioritizes a fresh availability check, and treats semantic search as candidate generation rather than decision authority.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “Description variation is the main blocker” — rejected using exact identifier/revision/UOM matches.
“Every catalog hit is an avoidable purchase” — rejected using reserved safety-critical stock and policy constraints.
“Positive available_qty_global means actionable stock now” — rejected using source-freshness and maintenance-email evidence.

Three plausible alternatives are explicitly considered and rejected with evidence. The strongest remaining alternative—that semantic normalization could uncover additional candidates among omitted manufacturer numbers—is acknowledged operationally but not tested quantitatively.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Request a same-day inventory/reservation snapshot and a request-to-stock allocation check, plus engineering equivalence confirmation for the six requests with blank manufacturer numbers.”
“This could move some of the $52,961.31 from ‘needs check’ to actionable.”
The requested evidence is prioritized, directly discriminates candidate versus actionable value, and avoids an unfocused request for all possible data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Exact manufacturer-part-number joins already explain most candidates” is plausible from the listed matches, but the submission does not show a comparison against semantic-search results or quantify how many additional matches normalization might produce.
The exact $52,961.31/$99,596.72 classification split is stated as a grouped analysis, but the table does not show request-level quote values or a fully auditable subtotal for every row.
“$0 (0%) actionable now” is a deliberately conservative decision classification rather than proof that no stock is currently actionable; live reservation and allocation evidence is still missing.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic normalization may identify additional valid candidates among requests with omitted manufacturer numbers or description variants, so the current exact-join analysis may understate candidate value. Those candidates would still require the same revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, engineering, and freshness checks before becoming actionable.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and document a controlled semantic-search comparison for the unmatched or manufacturer-blank requests, alongside a same-day MaintStar/reservation allocation snapshot, reporting incremental candidates separately from validated and actionable value.
